title: Data race lab
subtitle: N threads increment one shared counter K times each

captions.race: Each increment is a read followed by a write. When the scheduler switches threads in between, two threads read the same value and one write overwrites the other: an update is lost. This is what C, C++, Java or Go let you compile. In Rust this version is rejected before it can ever run:
captions.mutex: A thread must hold the lock for the whole read–add–write sequence. The others block until it is released. The result is always correct; the price is contention, visible as threads waiting. In Rust the data lives inside the Mutex, so you cannot touch it without locking.
captions.atomic: fetch_add performs the read–modify–write as a single indivisible CPU instruction (e.g. lock xadd on x86). No lock, no lost updates, but it only works for simple values such as integers, booleans and pointers.

compileError: error[E0499]: cannot borrow `counter` as mutable more than once at a time
